task.title: Implement automatic gate remediation retries
task.summary: Teach gateway/agency automation to treat actionable fail/block reports as same-loop remediation input, compile superseding outputs, and keep independent mid-roadmap decision workstreams parallel when safe.

goal.outcome: Agency can automatically remediate actionable gate fail/block feedback within policy/budget and can fence only dependent tasks when a new mid-roadmap decision appears.
acceptance: Gateway fail/block reports expose high-signal remediation payloads including exact refs, route, retry class, and stop reason when automation must stop.
Agency planning distinguishes retryable gate remediation from hard stop gates and schedules same-loop remediation only when scoped, safe, and within budget.
A blocked implementation/planning gate can lead to a superseding compiler/build recommendation without bypassing gateway promotion.
Mid-roadmap semantic decisions are modeled as parallel decision workstreams: dependent tasks are fenced, independent tasks remain schedulable.
Stop conditions still block non-actionable diagnostics, missing approval, artifact conflict, risk escalation, destructive/publication action, isolation policy failures, and budget exhaustion.
non_goals: Do not bypass gateway verdicts or mark work promoted on a blocked report.
Do not implement remote publication or destructive cleanup automation.

loop_start.reason: Compiler loops start from CodeWiki source refs; agents may refresh context when chat is noisy, stale, or token-heavy.

validation.reason: Implementation validation must not reuse builder thought context and must cite checked content proof.

next_loop.reason: The next gateway must independently validate implementation evidence and cite checked content proof.
